keyFindings.description: failedFallbackCopy settles a comment_fallback_copies row unpublished when its count reaches retry.DeadLetterAttempts (10). A failed row keeps its claim of now()+claimWindow (1 minute), so the copy is given up after about 10 minutes, and any decision error (Postgres) or non-ErrUnavailable publish error counts. An event never stops (backOff logs at the threshold and retries on retry.Delay; retry.go:13-16 says the events outbox does not stop because nothing about a publish failure is permanent). A transient outage of about 10 minutes therefore drops the only copy a mentioned session was owed. The PR body says 'as an event does'. Fix: back off on retry.Delay and keep retrying as an event does, logging once at the threshold.

A rollback to the previous build strands unsettled comment_fallback_copies rows: the previous build has neither the fallback pass nor the stranded pass, and the event is already published. The 0138 paragraph says the earlier release runs over the schema unchanged; name this and the drain check (select count(*) from comment_fallback_copies where settled_at is null).

recordFallbackCopies matches rows by (comment_id, destination, settled_at is null) and not by the claim it took, so a pass that outlasts claimWindow can release or fail a row another process has claimed since. The repeat publish carries the same dedupe key, so hosts drop it; guard on the claimed next_attempt_at.

Lines 480-487 restate the copy protocol and are now wrong (a resent mention's copy is not held back; it becomes a fallback row), naming mentionDeliveryQuery as the decider; point to publishFallbackCopies. Also: comment_delivery_sender_test.go:22-25 keeps a test copy of claimLease, and BroadcastPage.tsx:43,91 name the deleted claimLapsed.
